concept: Shy pieces advance around visible tracks only while occluded; bold pieces advance only while observed, so the player positions an eye and shutters to synchronize both kinds on sockets.
Hidden mills repeat the orientation in which they were last seen, making observation a write operation and occlusion the execution trigger.
Branching organisms grow only outside the observer cone; deliberate glimpses prune active tips and shape a path without touching the organism.
Tokens commit to a branch only when a junction is watched, but travel between junctions only when unseen, requiring alternating supervision and trust.
Creatures replicate when hidden and merge when illuminated; the target is a spatially displayed population distributed among enclosures.
Cargo transfers between paired pockets only while both endpoints are unobserved, while watched pockets lock and can serve as temporary storage.
Guards patrol while unseen and freeze under observation, whereas gates decay only while watched; crossing safely requires trading attention between threats and infrastructure.
Several cyclic mechanisms advance on a pulse only when their local conductor is occluded, and the player must align their phases without seeing every transition.
Objects inside a movable focus radius freeze while objects in the periphery flow, turning the boundary of attention into the main control surface.
Two movable observers jointly control pieces that respond to visibility by neither, either, or both observers, creating a small Boolean geometry of attention.
Autonomous walkers have stable yielding preferences; the player must infer who yields to whom and arrange encounters that untangle a crowded crossing.
Visually similar agents prefer different resource shapes, and only their choices reveal preferences needed for a later fair allocation.
A partner reacts to nonverbal spatial signals with an unknown but consistent policy that must be grounded through low-cost demonstrations before a joint route.
A group chooses its next corridor from recent gestures under an unknown aggregation rule, requiring inference of how individual signals become collective action.
Helpers remember whether the player recently assisted or obstructed them and reciprocate under a short, legible update rule.
The controlled body cannot perceive hazards, while an autonomous guide can and expresses safe directions through movement rather than symbols.
Some agents copy the player and others pursue latent destinations; efficient coordination depends on distinguishing imitation from goal-directed behavior.
Agents accept and reject shape bundles according to hidden partial orders, so the player must infer preferences and complete a cycle of mutually acceptable trades.
The player demonstrates a route to an apprentice whose imitation rule is incomplete, then adapts the lesson so the apprentice can finish alone.
Pedestrians follow one of several local social rules such as alignment, avoidance, or attraction; the player reshapes the crowd after identifying which rule is active.
An unseen wiring graph connects levers to lamps and gates; a small intervention budget forces experiments that distinguish several candidate graphs at once.
Moving one weight changes multiple platforms with unknown signs and ratios, and the player must identify the coupling before an irreversible loading phase.
Four visually symmetric machines hide one asymmetric causal link; carefully chosen probes expose the defect without testing every machine separately.
A finite bank of safe probes is followed by a single commit action, isolating experiment design from execution.
Turning any gear may drive several distant gears through hidden clutches, and only interventions reveal which apparent contacts actually transmit force.
The player chooses one seed and one barrier placement in a propagating field to produce an exact terminal pattern rather than merely a large reaction.
A lever affects whichever object currently occupies a hidden role, so interventions must separate object identity from causal position.
Local patches obey one of a few transformation laws; sparse probes must identify boundaries between laws before a global activation.
Cutting a connection is irreversible but reveals downstream flow, requiring a diagnostic sequence that preserves the one circuit needed for the goal.
Treating one node suppresses its neighbors and strengthens nodes two links away, so the player must infer the network from interventions before curing the exact target set.
Unknown machines split and merge a continuous-looking quantity while conserving total area, and the player routes exact shares into several receivers.
Pairwise transformations preserve an unseen parity class represented spatially, and the goal is reachable only after discovering the invariant.
Objects swap components rather than recolor independently, so every gain implies a loss elsewhere and planning requires global bookkeeping.
Shapes stretch, fold, and shear while preserving filled area; sockets care about area rather than silhouette.
Collisions redistribute directional motion among bodies, and the player must store and recover momentum to move a heavy object.
Flow divides across loops but the circulation sum remains fixed, letting the player infer invisible current from local indicators.
Allowed transformations change shape but preserve or predictably alter connected holes, making topology rather than pixel match the relevant invariant.
Adding mass to one node redistributes tension across a network with conserved total load and local capacity constraints.
Opposite charges are created and consumed only in pairs, and gates respond to net local charge rather than object count.
Visible silhouettes change with orientation while hidden mass stays constant, requiring the player to reconcile several projections before balancing platforms.
A movable aperture can reveal only a few cells per use, so the player chooses observations that identify a route instead of exhaustively exposing the board.
Limited pulses reveal distance rings but not direction directly; combining a few well-placed readings locates hidden obstacles.
A cart can sample the material beneath selected cells a fixed number of times before building a route over a heterogeneous floor.
Taking a snapshot preserves one region after it disappears, but a tiny snapshot bank forces the player to decide which evidence will matter later.
Disposable scouts reveal corridors until blocked, and choosing launch points determines whether enough map information survives for the main agent.
Each room permits one binary physical test whose outcome partitions several possible rule sets; later rooms demand increasingly informative tests.
Different sensors cost different amounts and reveal range, material, motion, or connectivity, so the player buys a minimal evidence set before acting.
Finite paint makes hidden boundaries visible permanently, turning information gathering into a spatial allocation problem.
The player may open a gate after any probe, but a wrong commitment destroys progress; optimal play stops when evidence is sufficient rather than exhausted.
Only a few observed patterns can be stored as reusable tiles, forcing selection of abstractions that explain later transformations.
Loose struts can be joined into rigid shapes whose geometry determines what gaps can be crossed and what loads can be supported.
Curved and flat fragments are assembled into an optical tool that redirects a beam according to the constructed surface, not a predefined tool type.
Threads woven across anchor points form traversable surfaces, with crossing and tension determining whether the bridge holds.
The player attaches a limited number of teeth to blank wheels to create transmission ratios that synchronize distant mechanisms.
Walls assembled from short segments create a funnel whose shape sorts moving particles by size and momentum.
Polar segments snap into a constructed chain whose alternating orientation creates a controllable attraction field.
Buoyant tiles are assembled into a footprint; stability, cargo placement, and narrow channels make the constructed geometry consequential.
Conductive pieces form an antenna whose span and orientation select which pulsing source can power a remote gate.
A mesh built from bars must pass small bodies while retaining large ones, then survive a later reversal of flow.
A small program of cams and delays is physically assembled to emit a required temporal action sequence after the player leaves.
Two controlled couriers occupy separate rooms and each sees clues needed by the other; actions also serve as the only communication channel.
One body sees objects while the other sees only their shadows, and solving requires aligning the two partial representations.
A switch in one room changes geometry visible only in another, so the player must maintain a shared causal state across alternating views.
Autonomous scouts return from hidden branches and communicate findings through short motion patterns that must be grounded.
One twin can see color and the other can see shape; control alternates and only joint evidence identifies valid objects.
Each agent sees only the nearest beacon, so a chain of agents must be positioned to transmit a global direction through local observations.
Several bodies hold overlapping but rotated map fragments, and movement decisions require registering them into one coordinate frame.
The body that controls motion sees only instruments while a passive observer sees the terrain and can signal with limited pulses.
Actions in one pane produce delayed echoes in another pane, and the panes expose complementary parts of the same hidden machine.
Three sensors each report only relative closeness through geometry; combining their views locates a moving hidden target.
A visible environmental phase changes which terrain grows or decays, and the player must revise a learned policy at predictable change points.
A guide alternates between copying and opposing the correct direction according to a detectable internal state rather than random deception.
The same material switches between solid-like and fluid-like interaction after accumulated energy crosses a visible threshold.
A movement transformation slowly rotates after each success, and sparse calibration actions reveal when the old mapping has expired.
A gate follows one learned activation rule until a visible wear cue appears, after which the complementary rule applies.
Heating and cooling the board changes which causal regime is active, making the player deliberately manage the rule set itself.
Tools change affordance after a known number of uses, so plans must anticipate functional aging instead of treating tools as permanent.
Autonomous agents cycle through a small set of response policies, with each transition signaled by their arrangement.
A general rule holds until a rare but legible marker announces a local exception, testing calibrated revision rather than wholesale abandonment.
Moving a control cart changes the physical law inside its radius, allowing the player to transport and compose rule regimes.
Several bodies exchange positions and appearances, but only persistent hidden identity determines which sockets they can activate.
Pieces temporarily acquire the color of containers while retaining their original interaction role, separating appearance from identity.
Objects split and merge, and later gates respond to ancestry rather than current shape or location.
Control jumps among bodies after contact while goals remain attached to bodies, requiring tracking controller and objective separately.
Footprints preserve which entity traversed a route even after entities become visually identical, enabling later assignment.
A duplicate copies appearance and position history but not learned permissions, and behavior reveals which is original.
Two agents swap physical capabilities while their individual destinations remain fixed, composing role reasoning with identity tracking.
Masks grant temporary affordances but accumulate obligations on the wearer, so passing a mask does not pass its debt.
A hidden passenger transfers between vehicles, and only the passenger can satisfy the final gate despite changing visible carriers.
Growing pieces inherit one of two latent traits through branching, and pruning must preserve the lineage needed at the end.
A final assembly implicitly requires several reusable subassemblies whose dependency order must be inferred from blocked interfaces.
Solving a room changes the boundary of a larger room containing it, revealing a hierarchy of local and global objectives.
Intermediate stable patterns unlock new growth operations, and the player must discover milestones rather than optimize immediate coverage.
Resources must flow through a branching dependency network where downstream requests reveal upstream subgoals.
Completing small cycles closes larger cycles, and the terminal objective is visible only through nested closure.
Temporary caches allow partial completion of repeated subtasks, rewarding discovery of reusable subgoal boundaries.
Machines accept outputs of other machines without semantic labels, requiring inference of a production hierarchy and scheduling within it.
Each rescued agent enables a distinct future action, so the apparent set of equal goals hides a dependency order.
Local navigation goals must be selected to create a reusable global route rather than merely approach the final target.
Opening a gate reveals a smaller instance of the same dependency pattern whose solution parameter controls the outer instance.
Pieces move in local coordinates on rotating rings while the target is fixed in global coordinates.
The room itself moves across a larger board, and the player navigates simultaneously within the room and through the world.
Directional controls pass through two independently rotating frames, each visually grounded by moving landmarks.
Objects move relative to belts that themselves move relative to the board, requiring composition of velocities in discrete time.
Small boards orbit a common center and exchange pieces only when local edge cells align globally.
Each region has a visibly oriented local gravity, and crossing a boundary changes the frame in which falling is predicted.
A map folds along visible hinges so distant local edges become globally adjacent without portal semantics.
Controls are relative to a movable camera while object dynamics remain world-relative, separating perception and action frames.
The maze rotates around the agent after each step, so stable landmarks must be tracked in a body-centered frame.
Portal exits are fixed relative to moving carriers rather than the global board, composing transport topology with reference frames.
A tutor demonstrates a short policy without highlighting goals, then control transfers on a visually transformed instance.
The player watches both a successful and failed attempt and must infer the discriminating rule rather than imitate surface motion.
Two tutors demonstrate different context-dependent policies, and the player identifies which context selects which tutor.
A demonstration contains one visible accidental action whose lack of causal effect must be separated from the intended policy.
Only the beginning and end of a successful trajectory are shown, requiring reconstruction of the latent subgoal sequence.
A sequence of examples gradually rules out candidate rules, and efficient learning depends on using counterexamples rather than majority resemblance.
After learning from a tutor, the player must demonstrate the rule to a simpler agent whose mistakes expose whether the abstraction was correct.
Different tutors each demonstrate one component of a policy that must be composed in a final room.
A policy demonstrated with flowing particles must transfer to a visually unrelated arrangement of moving blocks sharing the same causal graph.
Control transfers mid-demonstration and the player must continue the policy from the tutor's latent state rather than restart it.
A hunter predicts the player's most frequent recent direction under a small visible memory window, making deliberate habit-breaking useful.
An opponent commits toward the player's displayed intent before the player executes, rewarding a learnable two-stage feint.
Guards update patrol routes to block the player's last successful path, so repeating success is punished predictably.
A predator chooses among a few tactics based on the player's recent distance policy, and each tactic has a discoverable counter.
An adversary becomes more aggressive only after consecutive retreats, requiring controlled alternation rather than constant avoidance.
A rival imitates the player's previous action with a one-turn delay, and the player turns that adaptation into a remote actuator.
The opponent adopts the transformation rule that most recently defeated it, forcing transfer to a second strategy rather than brute persistence.
Patrol density shifts toward recently visited regions under a simple diffusion rule, making route diversity a planning resource.
An adversary learns which object the player approaches and protects it, so the player can teach it a false preference before committing.
A rival selects one of three timing patterns from the player's recent cadence, and irregular but planned timing opens a safe window.
Short and long spatial pulses acquire grounded meanings through partner reactions, then combine into multi-part route instructions.
Relative positions rather than colors or icons encode commands, forcing discovery of a small geometric communication protocol.
Signal order denotes destination while signal arrangement denotes action, and later commands require both dimensions.
Messages pass through agents that each transform signals by a learnable local rule, requiring composition across the relay.
A receiver reacts to the parity and grouping of pulses rather than their count alone, producing a nonverbal error-detecting code.
A channel predictably drops one class of signal, so redundant spatial encoding must be learned rather than repeated blindly.
Two partners begin with different signal mappings and converge only when the player establishes a consistent convention through feedback.
Primitive signals for object, direction, and timing can be concatenated into novel commands not demonstrated directly.
Senders and receivers operate on different visible cycles, so a valid message must encode both content and delivery phase.
The player invents reusable marker placements for latent object classes, and autonomous workers later act according to those grounded markers.
A visible ledger preserves the consequences of explored branches while the world resets, enabling comparison of alternatives before one irreversible commit.
Faint previews show where objects would move under each available action, but viewing a preview consumes a scarce resource.
The player may simulate one turn without committing, and later levels make choosing which turn to preview more important than the action itself.
A single reset is available across the whole level and preserves learned evidence but not progress, creating an explicit experiment-versus-execution split.
Two tiny copies of the same system can test different interventions before the chosen policy is applied to a larger irreversible system.
Opening any branch permanently seals its sibling, so the player must infer downstream compatibility before touching the fork.
Movable outlines predict whether a proposed tool or object arrangement would fit, allowing structural planning without actual construction.
Actions can be queued and inspected as a path before a single commit executes them all, but only one queue may be tested.
Abstract tokens stand for possible world models and are eliminated by observations; committing with multiple survivors risks the wrong transition.
Several uncertain routes have different worst-case losses, and the environment rewards preserving recoverability rather than shortest expected distance.
A flow-routing lesson is followed by autonomous traffic on a visually unrelated map with the same directed graph structure.
Occlusion patterns first teach a geometric relation that later reappears as invisible attraction between moving bodies.
Interleaving strands establishes a crossing algebra that transfers to temporal signal channels.
Population movement obeys the same conservation and capacity equations previously shown through fluid reservoirs.
A symmetry rule learned on shapes transfers to paired agents whose social roles mirror rather than their positions.
Physical bridge segments embody conjunction and disjunction, then the same structure governs activation without visible bridges.
Several levels preserve an exact causal graph while replacing every object's appearance, motion, and spatial embedding.
Two mechanisms share only the ordering of causes and effects, and a final level requires recognizing that abstract rhyme.
A rule learned among small objects inside one tile recurs among large regions across the whole board.
A tool's functional relation survives when its parts become autonomous agents, testing transfer from mechanics to social coordination.
The player may claim a hypothesis at any time; correct claims unlock efficient control while incorrect claims remove scarce actions.
Every turn offers either an information action or a progress action, making over-exploration and premature exploitation separately visible.
Physical evidence pieces accumulate with different reliability and must be placed on one of several hypothesis platforms before commitment.
A test sequence can continue indefinitely at a cost, but the environment rewards stopping once further observations cannot change the best action.
Candidate rules are represented by movable objects that can be retained or discarded, and recovery depends on not collapsing uncertainty too early.
The player chooses when to preserve state before a risky experiment; checkpoints are limited and reveal confidence through placement.
The same object can be safely probed or irreversibly used, with visual uncertainty shrinking as evidence accumulates.
Repeated noisy growth outcomes reveal stable likelihoods, and the player must allocate plants based on calibrated rather than absolute predictions.
Cargo with uncertain destination can be held, routed to a reversible hub, or committed down a one-way branch.
A visible evidence bar has no marked target; the player learns from feedback how much evidence different decisions require.
Stretching connected bands redistributes continuous-looking tension, and equilibrium rather than exact cell occupancy opens the gate.
Two fluids mix and divide through valves, with hue and area jointly conveying proportions without numeric notation.
Particle clouds move down a density gradient created by barriers, and the goal depends on shaping a distribution rather than individual paths.
Discrete pushes accumulate oscillation amplitude, and correctly phased pushes move a heavy body that no single action can shift.
A turn-based pendulum exposes its phase through position and momentum, requiring timed transfers between moving platforms.
Heat spreads locally after each turn and changes material affordances at visual thresholds, rewarding prediction of a field over time.
Pistons alter pressure across connected chambers, and balancing gradients moves membranes without rupturing them.
Pulses reflect and interfere on a network, with phase alignment at receivers rather than simple reachability determining success.
Rotating a few local vectors gradually aligns a global field whose integral direction controls object drift.
Only local changes in a smooth hidden field are visible, so the player performs efficient hill climbing while avoiding deceptive plateaus.
Every shortcut creates a delayed obstacle of the same shape elsewhere, linking local convenience to future geometry.
Tiles used in one room disappear from a later room, so an early path must conserve the material needed downstream.
Helping an agent changes its policy several rooms later, with intermediate rewards that can conceal the eventual effect.
Early placements alter a slowly evolving field that determines hazards only after multiple apparently unrelated subgoals.
Accepting temporary help creates a future obligation tied to the helper's identity, not the borrowed object.
An action is mirrored only after a visible countdown and in a different region, requiring plans that reserve future space.
Repeated use of an action gradually changes its later effect, making early action diversity relevant far beyond the current room.
The route walked in an early open field becomes the wall pattern of a later maze.
Resources and structural damage pass to a later controlled agent, so finishing the current level greedily can make the successor fail.
Opening one global shortcut permanently changes travel directions in every subsequent level, forcing a benchmark-wide planning choice.
Long deterministic animations contain a few causally important events, and the player must identify and act on event boundaries rather than individual frames.
Fast local cycles and a slow global cycle interact, requiring chunking repeated motion into higher-level phases.
A repeated action sequence can be packaged into one macro, but choosing the wrong abstraction hides a necessary branch.
Autonomous routines run until interrupted, and only state-defined windows permit a useful interruption.
A rhythm learned from one mechanism controls a slower mechanism after a simple scale transformation.
Several animations vary in duration but preserve causal event order, so timing by frames fails while timing by events transfers.
A single distinctive configuration anchors an otherwise repetitive cycle and enables long-horizon synchronization.
Later levels reward recognizing a familiar multi-action routine embedded inside a new plan without blindly replaying its final action.
Effects unfold across multiple frame sequences while new decisions remain available, requiring separation of pending and completed causes.
Several learned temporal abstractions compose into a final system where local events trigger transitions of a higher-level state machine.
